sundar.22.cau1: I know your greatness: you had a fight with Sahasrabāhu, and in battle with Vāli you won great fame. Hearing Hanumān's words, Rāvaṇa laughed them off.
sundar.22.cau2: I ate the fruit, my lord, because I was hungry, and being a monkey by nature I broke the trees. Everyone holds his own body most dear, master; those who walk the wrong path began to strike me.
sundar.22.cau3: I struck those who struck me, and for that your son bound me. Being bound does not shame me at all: I want to do my own Lord's work.
sundar.22.cau4: With joined hands I make this request, Rāvaṇa: put aside your pride and listen to my counsel. Think of your own lineage and see; give up your delusion and worship him who takes away his devotees' fear.
sundar.22.cau5: He is the one of whom even Death is sorely afraid, Death who devours gods, demons and all that moves and does not move: never make an enemy of him. At my word, give Sītā back.
sundar.22.do22: Śrī Rāma protects those who bow to him; he is an ocean of compassion, the slayer of Khara. If you go to him for refuge, the Lord will forget your offences and keep you safe.
sundar.23.cau1: Keep the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma in your heart, and hold unshaken rule over Laṅkā. The fame of the sage Pulastya is a spotless moon: do not become a blemish on that moon.
sundar.23.cau2: Without Rāma's name speech has no beauty; put away pride and delusion, reflect and see. Enemy of the gods, a fine woman decked with every ornament is not beautiful without clothes.
sundar.23.cau3: The wealth and power of one who has turned from Śrī Rāma slip away even as he holds them; to have them is as good as not having them. Rivers with no spring at their source dry up the moment the rains have passed.
sundar.23.cau4: Listen, Rāvaṇa, I say this on oath: for one who turns from Śrī Rāma there is no protector at all. Not even a thousand Śivas, Viṣṇus and Brahmās could save you, the enemy of Śrī Rāma.
sundar.23.do23: Give up the darkness of pride, which springs from delusion and brings much pain, and worship the Lord Śrī Rāma, Lord of the Raghus and ocean of mercy.
sundar.24.cau1: Though Hanumān had spoken words for his highest good, steeped in devotion, discernment, dispassion and right counsel, the arch-proud Rāvaṇa replied with a laugh: So we have found ourselves a monkey for a guru, and a very learned one.
sundar.24.cau2: Death has come close to you, wretch; that is why, vile creature, you set about teaching me. Hanumān said: It will be the other way round; I have seen plainly that your mind is deluded.
sundar.24.cau3: Hearing Hanumān's words, Rāvaṇa was greatly vexed and said: Why do you not take this fool's life at once? At this the demons ran to kill him, and just then Vibhīṣaṇa came with his ministers.
sundar.24.cau4: Bowing his head, he pleaded at length: Killing an envoy goes against right policy. My lord, give him some other punishment. All of them said: Brother, that is sound advice.
sundar.24.cau5: On hearing this Rāvaṇa laughed and said: Maim the monkey and send him back.
sundar.24.do24: Let me make it clear to you all: a monkey's heart is set on its tail. Steep cloth in oil, tie it round his tail, and then set it alight.
sundar.25.cau1: When the tailless monkey goes back there, the fool will bring his master here. Let me see the might of the one he has praised so much.
sundar.25.cau2: Hearing this, Hanumān smiled to himself: I see that Sarasvatī has come to help. The demons, hearing Rāvaṇa's words, set about that very plan, the fools.
sundar.25.cau3: Not a cloth, not a drop of ghee or oil was left in the city, yet the tail kept growing, for Hanumān was at play. The townsfolk came to watch the fun; they kicked him and laughed at him a great deal.
sundar.25.cau4: Drums were beaten and all clapped their hands; after parading him through the city they set his tail alight. Seeing the flames take hold, Hanumān at once made himself very small.
sundar.25.cau5: Slipping out of his bonds, Hanumān sprang up onto the golden upper storeys, and the demon women were struck with fear.
sundar.25.do25: At Śrī Hari's prompting, the forty-nine winds rose up at that very moment. Hanumān gave a great laugh and roared, and grew until he touched the sky.
sundar.26.cau1: His body was huge yet utterly light, and he ran leaping from one mansion to the next. The city burned and its people were in distress, as countless fearsome flames leapt and lunged.
sundar.26.cau2: Alas, father! Alas, mother! Such cries were heard: Who will save us now? We said so: this is not a monkey at all; it is some god who has taken a monkey's form.
sundar.26.cau3: Such is the fruit of slighting a holy man: the city burned like a city with no one to protect it. In the blink of an eye he burned the city down; only Vibhīṣaṇa's house did not burn.
sundar.26.cau4: He was the messenger of the one who created fire; that is why, Pārvatī, he did not burn. Turning this way and that, he burned the whole of Laṅkā, and then leapt down into the middle of the ocean.
sundar.26.do26: He put out his tail, shook off his weariness, took a small form once more, and stood with joined hands before Sītā, daughter of Janaka.
sundar.27.cau1: Mother, give me some token, as Śrī Rāma gave me one. Then she took off her crest-jewel and gave it to him, and Hanumān, son of the Wind, received it with joy.
sundar.27.cau2: Dear son, give him my obeisance and say this: My Lord, you are in every way fulfilled, wanting nothing. Keeping to your name as the one who is kind to the lowly, my Lord, take away my heavy affliction.
sundar.27.cau3: Dear son, tell the story of Jayanta, son of Indra, and make the Lord recall the might of his arrow. Should my Lord not come within a month, he will find me alive no more.
sundar.27.cau4: Tell me, Hanumān, how am I to stay alive? Now you too, dear son, speak of going. Seeing you brought my heart relief; now the same days and the same nights will be mine again.
sundar.27.do27: Hanumān comforted Sītā in many ways and gave her courage; then he bowed low at her lotus feet and set out to go to Śrī Rāma.
sundar.28.cau1: As he set out he gave a tremendous, thunderous roar; on hearing it, the demon women miscarried. He leapt across the ocean, came to this shore, and let the monkeys hear his cry of joy.
sundar.28.cau2: All were overjoyed to see Hanumān; the monkeys felt then that they had been born again. His face was glad and his body shone with splendour: he had done Śrī Rāma's work.
sundar.28.cau3: They all met him and were overjoyed, like a writhing fish that finds water. Joyfully they set off towards Śrī Rāma, asking about and recounting all that had newly happened.
sundar.28.cau4: Then they all went into Madhuvana and, with Aṅgada's leave, ate the sweet fruit. When the guards tried to stop them, they struck them with their fists, and the guards all ran away.
sundar.28.do28: They went and cried out: The crown prince is laying the grove waste. Hearing it, Sugrīva rejoiced: the monkeys had come back with the Lord's work done.
sundar.29.cau1: Had they not found news of Sītā, could they have eaten Madhuvana's fruit? The king was turning this over in his mind when the monkeys arrived with their whole company.
sundar.29.cau2: On arriving, they all bowed their heads at his feet, and the king of the monkeys greeted each of them with great love. He asked how they fared; they said: Seeing your feet, all is well; by Śrī Rāma's grace the task has gone exceptionally well.
sundar.29.cau3: My lord, it was Hanumān who did the work, and he saved the lives of all the monkeys. Hearing this, Sugrīva embraced him once more and set off with the monkeys to Śrī Rāma.
sundar.29.cau4: As Śrī Rāma watched the monkeys approach with the work done, his heart was filled with special joy. The two brothers were sitting on a slab of crystal; every one of the monkeys went up and fell at their feet.
sundar.29.do29: Śrī Rāma, compassion embodied, embraced them all with love and asked after their welfare. They said: My Lord, we are well now, having looked upon your lotus feet.
sundar.30.cau1: Jāmbavān said: O Lord of the Raghus, listen. One to whom you show mercy, my Lord, enjoys good fortune and well-being always and without end; gods, men and sages are pleased with him.
sundar.30.cau2: He alone is victorious and humble, an ocean of virtues, and his fair fame shines through the three worlds. By the Lord's grace the whole task has been accomplished; today our birth has borne fruit.
sundar.30.cau3: My Lord, what the son of the Wind has done could not be told even with a thousand mouths. Then Jāmbavān related to Śrī Rāma the splendid deeds of Hanumān.
sundar.30.cau4: As he heard them, they delighted the heart of the compassionate Lord, and joyfully he clasped Hanumān to his heart again and asked: Tell me, dear one, how does Sītā live, and how does she keep herself alive?
sundar.30.do30: Your name keeps watch day and night, meditation on you is the door, and her eyes, fixed on her own feet, are the lock: by what way could her life escape?
